profile.summary: A small Southland alpine shrub restricted to the Eyre and Thomson mountains and Mid Dome. It grows on rocky outcrops and in open snow-tussock grassland.
profile.lookFor: Pairs of fleshy oval leaves often edged red; flower spikes on noticeable stalks, with bright pink young buds or developing capsules.
profile.nameNote: NZPCN lists Hebe biggarii as a synonym and describes this range-restricted species as Naturally Uncommon. No Māori name was verified.

profile.summary: An endemic mountain shrub with several woody stems and dense narrow leaves. It occurs in scrub, tussock grassland, rocky alpine ground and mountain bogs.
profile.lookFor: Very narrow pointed leaves stand out from twigs and sheath them at the base; solitary white tubular flowers finish short side branches.
profile.nameNote: Inaka is a shared Dracophyllum name; NZPCN explicitly lists it for this species. NZPCN lists Dracophyllum uniflorum as a synonym.

profile.summary: An endemic small tree of lowland and mountain forest. Its large thin divided leaves give it a distinctive fan-like crown.
profile.lookFor: Usually seven finely toothed leaflets radiate from one point on a long stalk; cream flower sprays are followed by dark purple fruit.
profile.nameNote: The database spelling Scheflera digitata is retained. NZPCN and Flora of New Zealand verify Schefflera digitata, with a double f; those sources distinguish it from Pseudopanax five-finger.

profile.summary: An endemic woody climber that twines through shrubs and forest margins. Its leaves vary markedly in shape, especially on young plants.
profile.lookFor: Twining stems, clusters of fragrant pale tubular flowers and long thin pods that split to release tufted seeds.
profile.nameNote: The database spelling Parsonia heterophylla is retained; NZPCN and Flora of New Zealand verify Parsonsia heterophylla. Kaihua is documented by Flora of New Zealand. New Zealand jasmine is shared with other Parsonsia species.

profile.summary: A native prickly shrub of scrub and forest. Narrow stiff leaves and rounded fruit varying from white to red are useful recognition features.
profile.lookFor: Sharp-tipped narrow leaves with pale undersides; small cream flowers and white, pink or red berries.
profile.nameNote: Mingimingi is shared with several shrubs. NZPCN treats the New Zealand plant as Leptecophylla juniperina subsp. juniperina and lists Cyathodes juniperina as a synonym. The database Cyathoides juniperina spelling and its SP-060 relationship to SP-087 still need a WRT ruling. This profile illustrates the source taxon; it does not merge IDs, assign a nursery line to a subspecies or change SP-087’s zero recorded quantity.
